name: Question 5
problem: Given the inequalities $-3\le x<2$ and $x<1$, express their common set of solutions as an interval.
worked_solution:
We start by sketching the solutions to the two inequalities separately:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14191341/assets/7217f3db8adcbafdec9598e3c933fe1091e0abe9cabbdab57cca9cfb2d6cbb07.png)

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14191341/assets/690bb39741f157b12583ffffb75e47bcc171e04b7082f09005025f333807a234.png)

The common set of values consists of the values that are in both intervals. So, it can be graphed by finding where the two intervals overlap:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14191341/assets/d6ab3f0c43897adf0ae1b063d4d1d2437ce6d8f08355ff9f07a1e3e861e451b3.png)

Therefore, the common set of values is
$[-3,1).$
